svg.desc: Banner for a paper on the degree dependence of Houdré–Tetali isoperimetry. Title: The degree dependence of Houdré–Tetali isoperimetry. Subtitle: Simple graphs break the square-root Cheeger conjecture by a logarithm of the degree, and that is the worst case. Left: how much the spectral gap can lose, the comparison function Psi_p(Delta), the integral of t to the power minus 2p from 1 to Delta, plotted on a logarithmic scale against the boundary exponent p from 0 (vertex expansion) to 1 (conductance) for Delta = 2 to the 4, 2 to the 10 and 2 to the 20; a dashed line at p = one half marks where it equals log Delta. Centre: a ring of twelve tight neighbourhoods (cliques) joined by plain edges, with about M over r cubed wires at distance r, drawn as thicker lines between nearby neighbourhoods; a circulant graph. Right: for the square-root boundary, p = one half, plain graphs break the conjecture by a factor of order log(degree), and that is the worst case: for every walk the loss is at most 4 + log(1/kappa). For every exponent, 10 to the minus 8 times Psi_p(Delta) is at most the worst ratio, which is at most 12 times Psi_p(Delta). A mild effect: an upper estimate of the ratio is 0.50 at 260 vertices, 1.00 at about 1.7 times 10 to the 7 vertices and 1.55 at about 1.1 times 10 to the 12 vertices.
